arguments.rationale: Used all 10 successful forward calls. Baseline failures predominantly repeated already-completed arithmetic until the 32768-token cap. Matched-token short/long repetition probes revealed a cross-question residual drift. Selected edit applies W' = W - d(d^T W), using a normalized shared drift direction per layer, to attention-output and MLP-down projections in layers 7–18 only (24 internal tensors); no stop-token vector, embeddings, output head, final normalization, decoding change, training, or answer fitting. Head gains 0.5/2 and two query-gain caps worsened accuracy. Half/full drift projection scored 4/32 and 5/32 versus base 5/32 on the original set. The full projection then improved a separately selected, source-stratified 32-problem paired batch from 3/32 to 10/32, with 7 rescues and zero losses. Six of those rescues were genuinely completed correct mathematical answers; one scored correct while cut off. Across 64 paired problems the score is base 8/64 versus edited 15/64 (10 rescues, 3 losses); completed-correct counts are 7 versus 13. Independent validation, not reduced cutoffs alone, supports retention, although gains are modest, repetition remains frequent, and no held-out test evidence is claimed.
